mentl/a1a0ac8:
`delay(3)` emitted the one-slot register `delay(1)` emits. The authored
depth reached no reader at all, so a developer asking for a three-sample
delay silently got one — measured at the causality landing, where
delay(0), delay(1) and delay(3) each returned 30.

The depth is now read once, and every judgment about a feedback line is
an arm of that read. feedback_depth answers DepthLiteral / DepthComputed
/ DepthUnstated off the authored RHS; the causality refusal became one
arm of it (widened to n <= 0, since a negative literal cannot size a line
either), lower takes the slot count from the same read and carries it on
LFeedback(h, depth, body, spec), and the emit declares the line from that
number and shifts it by the same. One number, two readers, so a line can
no longer be emitted deeper or shallower than it is declared.

The line is a register file, not a ring: $s<h> newest through
$s<h>_<N-1> oldest, the prior read from the oldest — y[n-N] — and every
slot advancing one per tick, deep end first so each read precedes its own
overwrite. The shift pairs come from reversing the line and zipping it
against its own tail, so the walk is the line's own shape rather than an
index countdown. Nothing is allocated, so !Alloc survives at any N, and
state_slot_globals is the one projection both the plain module path and
the image substrate read — a persisted image now carries the whole line
instead of its newest slot.

A depth-1 line has no _i names and no pairs to shift, so it emits
byte-for-byte what it emitted before. Eleven delay(1) sites and five
accumulate sites crossed untouched and the march ruled CLEAN.

E_ComputedDelayDepth is armed at birth, the twelfth refusing class. A
depth no literal states cannot size a static line, and handing that site
one slot is the same silent wrong in a new costume. Census at arming: 0,
measured across src, lib, tests and examples.

mentl/a199109:
Root cause: infer.lux's ComposeExpr called resolve(ef) where ef
is an EfOpen effect variable. resolve() delegates to apply() which
only handles Ty constructors (TInt, TVar, TFun...) — EfOpen falls
through the match and returns Unit. This Unit propagated as the
effect row in the composed TFun, causing unify_eff to crash when
the composed function was later called.

Fix: don't resolve effect variables through the type substitution.
Leave them as-is in the TFun — resolve_type handles them later via
apply_eff_subst when the full type is resolved.

Also: replaced codegen's synthetic-AST desugaring with direct
bytecode emission (builds FnProto inline, no synthetic LambdaExpr).

Phase 1 of the throne roadmap: compose scope bug — COMPLETE.

DESIGN_DIRECTION audited the art and closed out. This is the match, and
the surfaces you touch to reach one. Six findings, each cited to the line
that proves it; the operator's play report (couch + network) is treated
as primary evidence and the code read to explain it.

The headline was felt from the seat before it was read in the source:
the clock is vestigial. It is worse than vestigial. MatchScore is a
cumulative kill counter that reset_round_state deliberately never
touches, and tick_match_state ends the match on 5 kills checked
identically in InRound and RoundOver -- so a round expiring changes
nothing on the scoreboard. The boundary costs 240 frames (4.0 s of
RoundOver plus 3-2-1) and buys nothing. And it is not neutral: the one
piece of state it does touch is CatchStreak, which it deletes, so the
clock's only gameplay effect is to punish the player who built the
perfect-catch ladder. The sudden-death crumble squeezes both players
toward a buzzer with no stakes behind it. MATCH_WIN_THRESHOLD's own
comment concedes the divergence from BUILD_PLAN's "first to 5 round
wins" and calls it satisfied in spirit; round wins and cumulative kills
are different games. Three exits are costed, cheapest first; all bump
SIM_VERSION, which argues for doing it once.

stoop/a182109:
Every repaint of the press measured the pages at scale one for a moment,
the browser pulled the scroll back to fit that shorter page, and nothing
put it back: clicking a cutting on page six threw the view up to page
three and the cutting off the screen. The scroll is kept through the
measurement now, in the press and in the file's own pages.

A cutting drags freely across the gutter of a spread, both pages
repainting as it goes, and can be duplicated, with Ctrl-D or a button, or
sent to the page before or after. A piece too long for its page runs on to
the next, each page measured in the press itself, with a line saying where
the rest went and the heading carried over; a few words over stays a trim
for the fit meter to ask for, not a page of its own. A page's photograph
takes its room from the PNG header before the browser decodes it, so the
measurement is true the moment the page is painted.

A faint line on each page shows where a home printer stops reaching,
drawn only along the edges that meet the edge of the sheet, which depend
on the fold and move when it is swapped. Screen only; the print is
another sheet.
